beats.headline: Welcome to your farm!
beats.body: Old Joe’s farm is yours now. The vegetables are ripe, the stand is open and the village is already queueing.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Pick what's ripe, fill the stand, and never keep a neighbour waiting. Everyone here knows everyone.

beats.headline: Sweet corn is growing!
beats.body: The village says it’s the sweetest they’ve ever tasted. Corn takes longer to grow, but it sells for more.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Corn takes its time, but folk pay more for it. Keep both fields busy.

beats.headline: The hens have moved in!
beats.body: Four hens, one bright red hen house, and fresh eggs for the stand. People are stopping by just for them.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Collect them while they're warm and pack them six to a carton. Happy hens, happy customers.

beats.headline: Someone’s minding the stand!
beats.body: A friendly face now serves the customers all day, so you can get out into the fields.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Now you're farming like an owner. Let your helper sell; you keep the crates coming.

beats.headline: A farmhand joins the crew!
beats.body: They pick the fields and carry the crates to the stand. The farm has never been so busy.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Good help is worth every penny. The farm runs itself while you plan what's next.

beats.headline: The big red barn is up!
beats.body: There’s room for crates by the dozen, and your produce has never been fresher.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: I always dreamed of a barn like that. You did it proper.

beats.headline: The feed store is open!
beats.body: Your own corn becomes animal feed. Well-fed hens lay twice as fast, and the cows give more milk.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Every crate of corn in that hopper comes back as eggs and milk. Keep it topped up and the animals will do the rest.

beats.headline: Your farm has a sign!
beats.body: It hangs over the gate, and people from the next valley are driving over for your eggs, milk and veg.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: A good sign brings folk from miles around. Now feed those animals proper and they'll give you twice as much.

beats.headline: A cow has moved in!
beats.body: She has a brand-new cow barn (with room for two more), and there’s fresh milk to sell.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Milk them gently and bottle it cold. Nothing sells like fresh milk.

beats.headline: Rex Goldsby is back!
beats.body: His Goldsby Agri is selling cheap to the village, and fewer shoppers are stopping at your stand. A milk tanker of your own should see him off.
beats.speaker: rival
beats.words: Deliveries? Cute. My trucks are bigger.

beats.headline: Goldsby Agri has left the valley!
beats.body: Your milk tanker delivers fresher milk than anyone’s. Rex has sold his farms and gone. How about an orchard next?
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Better service beats a bigger truck. Now, a few apple trees down by the lane would do nicely...

beats.headline: A heatwave has hit!
beats.body: Gardens all over the village have dried up. For the next three minutes people pay double for anything fresh.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: When the gardens dry up, folk come to us. Keep that stand full!

beats.headline: Rain at last!
beats.body: The fields are green again, and you kept everyone fed while the valley was parched.

beats.headline: Six apple trees are planted!
beats.body: Once they blossom they fruit again and again. The village is already asking about apple pies.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Trees are patient business. Plant them, wait, and they pay you every year after.

beats.headline: The bakery is open!
beats.body: Your corn becomes warm bread and your apples become pies. Bread sells for twice what the corn did.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Corn is cheap, bread is not. Every step you add to a crate is money in your pocket.

beats.headline: The farmers’ market is open!
beats.body: Striped stalls, fresh food and music by the road. Shoppers come from all over the valley, and they pay top prices.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: People come for the food and stay for the fun. Keep those stalls full!

beats.headline: The windmill is turning!
beats.body: The village held its fair under the sails, and every shop in the valley is busier for it. Now, what about that old Starlight fairground across town?
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: You've made this valley proud. Mabel rode the carousel at the old Starlight fairground as a girl. It's been closed twenty years. The land's for sale, if you can raise the money.
